title: UI tests with Testing Library: querying by role and label

objectives.text: Render a component in a test with React Testing Library and find elements with getByRole by accessible name and with getByLabelText
Choose getBy, queryBy or findBy for an element that is present, absent or appears asynchronously
Simulate typing and clicking with user-event and assert on what the user can see

minutes.basis: Measured on the authored artifact.html with the frozen estimator (authoring/tools/timing/estimate_reading.py): P50 7.17 minutes. Worst required path models one additional wrong graded attempt per interactive unit before it settles, at the estimator cost table (1 predict at 30 s, 1 explore at 20 s, 3 terminal_step at 35 s, 1 mcq at 45 s): 10.5 minutes. Budget and about label are 11: the larger of the intake plan of 10 and ceil(max(P50, worst path)), under the 15-minute ceiling (authoring/docs/tools/validators.md). This is a model, not a measurement with learners. Re-synced 2026-11-20 after a learner-text wording pass: estimator P50 7.17 -> 7.22; modeledWorstPath shifted by the same delta (10.5 -> 10.55); budget and aboutLabel unchanged.

pdf.reason: Not applicable: core topic; a PDF is present only for Reading topics and topics that declare a print handout

lab.reason: No topic lab. Standard practice of all three objectives is task 8 of the module lab react/forms-context-and-crud/coding-lab/ on S33, where tasks 4-8 run: the learner writes their own test for the named blank-then-valid ServiceForm scenario. npm test machine-scores that test's behaviour by rerunning it against an unchanged control and six faulty runtime variants of the learner's form, so vacuous and partial tests are rejected; the role and label queries (#o1), the getBy/queryBy/findBy choice (#o2) and the user-event interaction (#o3) are self-checked practice, not machine-verified. Course project: applied in part P5 of the planned cumulative course project react/coding-lab/ (Standard S33 Build block and Fast FT20 increment), after an embedded teach-then-check step; authored in a course-level PR
